text: Every defense this course has built reduces the odds and shortens time-to-detection. None of them makes failure impossible. Incident response is the plan for the day one happens anyway.

Detect — an alert fires or a user reports it. Triage — how many affected, is it still happening. Contain — roll back, tighten, or disable. Communicate — tell affected users honestly. Review — which control should have caught this?

The AI-specific wrinkle is mostly containment. Unlike a traditional bug, there's often no single line of code to revert — it might mean rolling back a model version or disabling the feature while a real fix is built.

A harmful hallucination — add it to the eval dataset immediately. A prompt injection that got through — patch it, then re-run red-teaming for siblings. A valid bias complaint — treat it as a signal the tests missed something.
A postmortem's real job is closing the loop back into evals, alerts, or documentation. An incident that doesn't change any of those was reviewed, not learned from. Next: the capstone.
